newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo cars drive first-quarter profits up. [CORRECTED 19:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Volvo cars drive first-quarter profits up. [CORRECTED 19:10 GMT]

text.p: Swedish vehicle maker AB Volvo said Wednesday that its car business helped it post a better-than-expected 60 percent increase in operating profits in the first three months of the year.

Volvo said its operating profits rose to 1.89 billion crowns ($247 million), led by the cars division, where operating profits soared to 1.07 billion crowns ($139.7 million) after a loss of 191 million crowns ($24.9 million) in the same period a year ago.
(Corrects dollar conversion to $24.9 million from $249.3 million).

"This was a very good report, particularly on the car side," analyst Philip Ayton from BZW said. "Volvo had a very good fourth quarter last year but it was not clear if this was a one-off or a new trend. It now appears to be a new trend and will have some impact on the full year."

Volvo's first quarter sales rose to 41.85 billion crowns ($546 million) from 39.07 billion ($510 million) a year earlier, pumped up by car sales that rose 18 percent to 23.07 billion crowns ($301 million).
The number of cars invoiced rose to 94,500 from 85,200.

However, Volvo's truck sales fell 6 percent to 10.94 billion crowns ($143 million) while the unit's operating profit fell to 304 million crowns ($39.7 million) from 731 million crowns ($95.4 million) in 1996, hit by smaller margins and volumes of sales in Europe.
The problems in this division had been known in the market for nearly a year and were factored into the market view of Volvo. Analysts said the truck results were as expected.
"Volvo Truck is still being charged with losses in the North American operations," outgoing chief executive Soren Gyll said in a statement.
"Vigorous measures are underway to restore the profitability of the U.S. business. Volvo Trucks' profits in Europe continue to be good."
Volvo's pre-tax profit soared to 5.25 billion crowns ($685 million) from 1.92 billion crowns ($251 million), which was above market expectations.
However this sum included a capital gain of 3.03 billion crowns ($396 million) from the sale of shares in drinks group Pripps Ringnes.
